messages.subject: Re: cbind datasets of different length
parts:
Looks like the following is what you're after...

http://ryouready.wordpress.com/2009/01/23/r-combining-vectors-or-data-frames-of-unequal-length-into-one-data-frame/

Well this works but it would be much more convenient to get this done in one single function and well, since october 2008 there is one. It can be found in the plyrpackage written by Hadley Wickham. So the solution is as easy as:

library(plyr)
l <- myList
do.call(rbind.fill, l)

# another example

l <- list(data.frame(a=1, b=2), data.frame(a=2, c=3, d=5))
do.call(rbind.fill, l)

The results:

  Intercept  x1  x2  x3
1       0.4 0.4 0.2 0.7
2       0.5  NA 0.8  NA

Now, this is nice! It is really worthwhile having a look at Hadley Wickhams plyrpackage as it provides a lot of functions that make life a lot easier when it comes to splitting list or data frames, doing a calculation or not and merge them afterwards again. More on that another day.

Cheers, Mark
